title: Why Spielberg Said 'No' to Harry Potter and Made a Robot Movie Instead
summary: What if the first Harry Potter movie had been directed by Steven Spielberg? It almost happened! Back in the late 1990s, when the Harry Potter books were becoming a huge deal, Spielberg was picked to turn the first book into a movie. But he walked away. Why? Because he had promised his friend, the famous director Stanley Kubrick, that he would finish Kubrick's dream project: a movie called A.I. Artificial Intelligence. Kubrick had worked on the story for years but died before he could make it. At Kubrick's funeral, his wife asked Spielberg to take over. So Spielberg said goodbye to Hogwarts and hello to a futuristic tale about a robot boy who wants to be real. The movie came out in 2001, just months before Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone hit theaters. Spielberg recently said he was further along on Harry Potter than people knew—he even had a script! But he doesn't regret his choice. A.I. is a strange, beautiful, and sometimes creepy film that has become a cult classic. It's about love, loss, and what it means to be human. Harry Potter, of course, became a massive hit under director Chris Columbus. But Spielberg's decision led to a string of bold, personal movies in the early 2000s. Sometimes the best adventures are the ones nobody expects.
why_it_matters: Sometimes sticking to a promise is more important than taking the biggest opportunity, and that can lead to creating something special and unexpected.
